items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I had met Dick when we were playing the Apollo Theater.

ctx.x: And my wife's father died. And I left and went to New York to the funeral. While in New York, I decided to go

by and see a fellow named Dick Campbell who was the coordinator of talent for the USO camp shows. I had met Dick when we were playing the Apollo Theater. So I went down to the USO camp shows, and Dick was glad to see me. And he said, "By the way, Pillars, how would you like to come with the USO?" He says, "We'll keep you in the States a few weeks, and then maybe we'll send you to Europe." I said, "It's a good deal." He says, "When can you join the band?" I said, "Well, we're working at the Club Plantation now.…

He says, "Okay, I'll tell you what I'll do. I'll book you, put you on the train, we'll get Pullmans for you, put you on the next morning, you'll get on the train, and you'll come on out to New York and we'll process you for USO." Sent us the contract and we signed it. We finished that night, Labor Day night, got on the train the next day, everybody had a lower berth except my wife and I. And I wanted it that way. I told them, I said, "You fellows take the lower berths. My wife and I, we'll take an upper berth."…
